## Context / Problem
The runner attaches per-call usage to every result (`result["_usage"]`, src/rebar/llm/runner.py:543) but Pass-1 discards it: passes.pass1_chunk, passes.pass1_container, and passes.pass1_isf return findings lists only, so BatchRunResult.outputs (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:167-176) carries no usage key and plan-review coverage.metrics has call counts but no token totals for the most expensive pass (the gap is documented at src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:139-149; _attach_plan_review_metrics currently reconstructs only det_ms/llm_ms/llm_calls timing proxies). Per-criterion request counts are extracted (runner.py:_extract_usage) but never persisted, blocking data-driven criterion demotion decisions.

## Approach
run_pass1 does not call runner.run directly — calls flow through _chunk -> sizing.pass1_with_ladder -> passes.pass1_chunk (and the container/ISF variants). The usage is threaded through that chain as a coordinated API change with EVERY caller updated atomically in this one change. The three pass functions have consumers outside the plan_review package, all enumerated and updated here: the in-package chain (sizing.pass1_with_ladder chunk path, pass1._chunk, pass1's container fan-out via _timed_pairing, pass1's ISF invocation) plus src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py (pass1_container at line 120, pass1_chunk at line 137), src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py (pass1_chunk at line 345), and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py (pass1 calls and the run_focused_finder 2-tuple destructure at line 344) — the eval/preview call sites unpack and discard the new usage element (`findings, _usage = ...`). Specifics: (1) passes.pass1_chunk, passes.pass1_container, and passes.pass1_isf change return type from list[dict] to (list[dict], dict) — findings plus the call's _usage dict; _timed_pairing keeps its existing (findings, pairing_record, exc) triple — the container call's usage is embedded as pairing_record["usage"] so the observability record and the accumulator read one field. summarize_for_isf (passes.py:525-541) is a mode="text" single-turn call returning a plain string (str(runner.run(req).get("text", ""))) — it cannot return a pair without breaking its string contract, so it is handled differently: it changes to capture the full runner result internally and return (text, usage_dict), and its sole caller (the ISF oversized-log path in pass1.py) unpacks the pair and appends a call record attributed to the ISF criterion with criteria=["ISF"]. sizing.pass1_with_ladder's two pass1_chunk call sites (the direct-return path at sizing.py:316 and the out.extend escalation path at sizing.py:333) both unpack the new pair and merge usage records. The concurrent-futures collector at pass1.py:490 changes from findings.extend(fu.result() or []) to unpacking: each future resolves to (findings_list, usage_records); the collector extends findings and appends the records. (2) Checkpoint fast-path: when sizing.load_checkpoint serves a chunk from cache, no LLM call happened — the chunk contributes NO call record and zero usage (a test asserts a checkpoint-resumed chunk adds nothing to the aggregate). Aggregation protocol: usage is recorded per CALL as {criteria: [ids the call covered], requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens} — no llm_calls field on a per-call record (one record IS one call); the per-criterion llm_calls value is DERIVED as the count of call records covering that criterion. Ladder retries: every COMPLETED attempt pass1_with_ladder makes for a chunk appends its own call record, all carrying the same criteria list. An attempt that RAISES (e.g. the context-limit error that triggers escalation) returns no result dict, so its usage is not recoverable from the current runner API — such attempts contribute nothing, and this limitation is documented in the accumulator's docstring; recovering usage from raising calls is explicitly out of scope. run_pass1 derives (a) the aggregate sum over all call records and (b) a per-criterion map using this attribution rule: an AGENT call (single criterion) attributes wholly to that criterion; a multi-criterion single-turn chunk attributes its token fields divided equally across its covered criteria (a documented approximation — the sidecar retains the raw per-call records, so exact attribution is always reconstructable), while the derived per-criterion llm_calls and the requests field count in full for each covered criterion. (3) The prerequisite finder runs in ProductionBatchRunner.run() via prerequisites.run_focused_finder, which returns (records, findings) with no usage — it is extended to return (records, findings, usage) where usage is the SUM over every runner.run call its internal run_bin closure makes (run_bin is recursive and multi-call; each call's _usage is accumulated inside run_focused_finder), its callers updated in the same change — ProductionBatchRunner.run and the fidelity_spot_eval.py destructure (scope includes src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py), and that usage is merged into the aggregate before emitting BatchRunResult.outputs["_usage"]. (4) _attach_plan_review_metrics (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:249+) is EXTENDED to fold the new token totals from the batch step output into coverage.metrics alongside its existing timing fields. (5) The sidecar payload (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py build_payload) gains coverage.usage = {"per_call": [call records], "per_criterion": {id: map}} — these exact key names are what the tests assert. Alternative rejected: post-hoc parsing of the REBAR_USAGE_LOG JSONL — opt-in, not always present, and not keyed by criterion.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py, src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py (new, beside tests/unit/workflow/test_production_batch_runner.py).

## Testing
FakeRunner.run does not emit _usage (runner.py:134-151), so tests use a thin test-local wrapper runner that delegates to FakeRunner and attaches deterministic stub _usage dicts to each result — no change to FakeRunner itself. Unit with that wrapper: aggregate totals equal the sum over chunk, agent, container, ISF, and prerequisite call records; a two-criterion chunk with 100 input tokens attributes 50 to each criterion while counting one llm_call for each; a simulated ladder escalation whose first attempt completes yields two call records both counted, while a first attempt that raises contributes no record; coverage.usage.per_call and coverage.usage.per_criterion appear in the sidecar payload with the documented key names; coverage.metrics gains the token totals through the extended _attach_plan_review_metrics; a runner result without _usage degrades to zeros; the full existing pass1/batch-runner suites pass with the new return shapes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a review, coverage.metrics contains input/output/cache token totals that include Pass-1 and prerequisite calls (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py` summing FakeRunner stub usage).
- [ ] The sidecar payload carries coverage.usage.per_call (raw call records with criteria lists) and coverage.usage.per_criterion under exactly those keys (checked: sidecar payload unit test).
- [ ] A multi-criterion chunk divides token fields equally across its criteria and counts llm_calls in full per criterion; ladder-retry attempts each contribute a call record (checked: dedicated unit tests for both rules).
- [ ] Missing _usage on any call degrades to zero contribution (checked: unit test).
- [ ] Every caller of the three changed pass functions and of run_focused_finder — including eval_solver.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, and criterion_preview.py — is updated in this change and the existing pass1, batch-runner, eval, and finalize test suites pass unmodified in behavior (checked: full `pytest tests/unit/` run).
- [ ] A checkpoint-resumed chunk contributes no usage and run_focused_finder's usage equals the sum over its internal run_bin calls (checked: dedicated unit tests).
